top_story: A reported projectile strike on an LPG tanker in the Strait of Hormuz on 17 November pushed maritime insecurity back to the center of the Gulf, threatening a chokepoint that directly shapes fuel flows, insurance costs, and civilian livelihoods across the region. Hours later in the occupied West Bank, the killing of a 72-year-old Palestinian woman near Jericho during an alleged settler attack underscored how unchecked local violence continues to deepen fear and displacement far from formal front lines. By 18 November, the US sentencing of Asif Merchant for a plot to kill Donald Trump in retaliation for Qassem Suleimani’s killing revived the long afterlife of US-Iran confrontation, linking episodic transnational revenge plots to a broader climate of escalation. Together, these developments show a region where strategic rivalry and localized violence reinforce each other, widening insecurity from shipping lanes to village doorsteps.
